preview_text: England topped Group L with nine points, sealing their place in the Round of 32 with a 2-0 win over Panama. Jude Bellingham scored in the first half and Harry Kane converted in the second, with Jordan Pickford keeping his third clean sheet of the tournament.

Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice both served as corner kick delivery sources throughout the group stage. England were held scoreless in their first two group games before a pair of goalless first halves — they have yet to score in the first half of a World Cup match at this tournament.

England conceded zero goals across all three group games, the only side alongside Mexico to keep three clean sheets. Harry Kane has scored in the tournament and brings 43 international goals into the Round of 32.

Harry Kane headlines England's DFS pool as the highest-opto player and team captain at the attacking tip, while Jordan Pickford provides clean-sheet value in goal at a salary well below most competing goalkeepers on this slate.

DR Congo qualified for the Round of 32 as one of the best third-placed teams after a dramatic 3-1 comeback win over Uzbekistan in their final group game. Yoane Wissa converted a penalty to tie it, and scored again late with a solo effort.

Arthur Masuaku served as DR Congo's corner kick taker and left back throughout the group stage. Yoane Wissa has been the most productive attacking player in the group stage, providing the crucial goals to secure knockout qualification.

DR Congo came from behind against Uzbekistan after being one goal down in the first half. Their three-goal second-half performance was the most dramatic recovery of any qualifying side's final group game.

Yoane Wissa is the only viable DFS option from DR Congo with tournament-proven goal output as the team's primary forward threat. Lionel Mpasi provides budget goalkeeper value with clean sheet potential against a limited England attack that has yet to score in the first half of a World Cup match at this tournament.

Belgium topped Group G with seven points after finishing with a commanding 5-1 win over New Zealand in their final group game. Leandro Trossard scored in that match, adding to his group stage tally and confirming his place as a key attacking threat.

Kevin De Bruyne served as Belgium's primary corner kick taker as the team's playmaking fulcrum. Maxim De Cuyper also contributed from set pieces at left back and is the second corner kick taker in the AO data.

Belgium registered five goals against New Zealand after two consecutive draws, showing genuine depth in their attacking unit. Their group stage totaled seven goals from multiple scorers, with De Bruyne involved in the majority of attacking moves.

Kevin De Bruyne anchors the Belgium DFS stack as the highest-ownership player at his salary tier with corner kick volume and direct attacking output. Maxim De Cuyper provides a budget stacking option at left back with corner exposure.

Senegal advanced as one of the best third-placed teams after a historic 5-0 win over Iraq, the biggest win ever by an African nation at a World Cup. Habib Diarra scored in the fourth minute and Ismaila Sarr added his third goal of the tournament in the 56th minute off a Lamine Camara assist.

Lamine Camara and El Hadji Malick Diouf served as corner kick takers throughout the group stage. Sadio Mane drew the red card that gave Senegal a man advantage against Iraq, and has been a constant threat even without adding to the scoresheet.

Ismaila Sarr leads Senegal with four goals in the group stage, the most by any player at this tournament from a third-placed qualifier. Pape Gueye scored twice as a substitute against Iraq, both from long range, with his second reaching 132km per hour.

Ismaila Sarr leads Senegal in DFS value with four goals and consistent involvement throughout the group stage. Iliman Ndiaye offers upside off his long-range group stage finisher and attacking positional freedom.

The USA topped Group D with seven points, winning their first two matches before fielding a heavily rotated lineup in a dead-rubber 2-3 loss to Turkey. Christian Pulisic returned from injury in that match as a second-half substitute. Their key performances came in wins over Paraguay and Australia.

Folarin Balogun scored twice against Paraguay in Round 1 and has led the USA attack throughout the group stage. Christian Pulisic serves as primary corner kick taker when fit and in the starting lineup, as does Malik Tillman and Antonee Robinson from their respective positions.

The USA scored eight goals across the group stage, a program record for a single World Cup. Balogun leads with two goals in the tournament while Alex Freeman and Sebastian Berhalter scored against Turkey in the rotated lineup.

Folarin Balogun is the top USA DFS asset with two group stage goals and the highest opto percentage among forward options. Antonee Robinson provides corner kick upside at left back with strong attacking output throughout the tournament.

Bosnia and Herzegovina qualified for the Round of 32 as one of the best third-placed teams with four points. They drew with Canada in Round 1 before losing 1-4 to Switzerland, then beat Qatar 3-1 in their final group game to clinch qualification.

Kerim Alajbegovic and Ivan Basic have served as corner kick takers in Bosnia's group stage matches. Edin Dzeko brings veteran international experience at the forward line alongside Ermedin Demirovic as the primary attacking partnership.

Bosnia's 3-1 win over Qatar in Round 3 confirmed their place as the first third-placed team to qualify from the 2026 group stage. Esmir Bajraktarevic has been their most dynamic offensive contributor in wide areas, while Ermin Mahmic scored in the tournament.

Esmir Bajraktarevic offers the best DFS value from Bosnia as a dynamic wide midfielder at a mid-range salary, while Edin Dzeko provides veteran goal threat at forward as the nominal attacking reference point.
